title: IN THE HIVES MYSTERY, ANSWERS AREN'T EXACTLY BREAKING OUT ALL OVER
question_only:
sometimes when i am near my wife she breaks out in hives. but then, betty also suffers an occasional bout of hives when i am not around, so my role in her hives may be negligible.
then again it may not be. that's the thing about hives. for some people they are totally predictable: eat strawberries and get hives. but for many others, hives is an annoyance that strikes as mysteriously as love.
maybe that's it: i am so lovable that i give betty hives. a mother wrote to dear abby some time ago and said that her son howard gave her hives whenever he came home from college. abby told her not to let howard move back home when he graduated.
for howard's benefit, and maybe mine, but more for those around us who get hives, here is a basic rundown on the ailment and some of what is available as treatment.
hives are itchy patches of raised bumps on the skin. these are called wheals, and they range from freckle size to several inches across.
it is estimated that 10 percent to 20 percent of the u.s. population suffers from acute hives at some time. usually these are brief, scattered encounters that can be traced to a precise cause: taking medication such as penicillin or aspirin or from eating such foods as strawberries or shellfish.
part of the obvious treatment for such hives is to avoid the cause, said dr. richard vandellen, a consultant in allergy diseases at the mayo clinic.
the mechanics of this type of hives are similar to an allergic reaction in which skin cells release antibodies, vandellen said. one of the antibodies is histamine, hence the wide use of antihistamines in allergy and hives treatment.
for those who suffer from chronic hives, and their numbers are small compared to victims of the acute type, the cause and effect are not so simple. usually it is impossible to pinpoint what causes the hives, and about all the victims can do is seek treatment.
"with a few rare exceptions," vandellen said, "we can find a drug or a combination of drugs that will give them relief."
chronic hives, according to vandellen and other mayo doctors, may be caused by infections, exposure to heat or cold, medications such as aspirin or aspirin substitutes called ibuprofen, emotional upset or food additives such as dyes, preservatives and sulfites.
"there may be a different mechanism at work than in acute hives," vandellen said. "we really don't know yet, but a similiar treatment approach, using antihistamines, is the best we can do at this point."
there are many antihistamines available, some of which are known by the trade names benadryl, vistaril, atarax and periactin.
another antihistamine called terfenadine, with the trade name seldane, has been widely used to treat hives in europe, but the food and drug administration has approved its use only for allergy treatment, vandellen said. its advantage over other antihistamines is that it does not cause as much drowsiness. u.s. approval for use against hives is pending.
inducing a certain amount of drowsiness may, however, be important to successful treatment in some cases because it helps alleviate symptoms, according to dr. henry roenigk, chairman of the dermatology department at the northwestern university medical school.
though seldane is getting much publicity, roenigk said he thinks the dermatology community does not consider it as much of a breakthrough as the manufacturer contends.
the drug doxepin, with the trade names sinequan and adapin, is also being used with success. this is an antidepressant, vandellen said, and is sometimes used to treat hives that resist other drugs.
there is another kind of hives called dermographia in which the skin erupts in response to being stroked with a fingernail or pencil. my daughter pat has this condition occasionally. it is the skin's reaction to pressure and involves the same physical mechanics as other hives.
as for itching in regard to hives: do you scratch or don't you, given that the urge to do so, according to my wife, is sometimes enough to drive you to kick the furniture?
you don't, according to vandellen.
"scratching will probably just make hives feel worse," he said, "and in some cases hives are so widespread that scratching is impractical anyway."
"you can apply a cortisone cream or cold tap-water compresses," he said.
"be patient," vandellen advises hives sufferers. "in almost all cases, the hives will go away eventually."
hives, though they are most commonly only an irritation, can also be painful and disabling, particularily if they occur on the palms or on the soles of the feet.
there is also a rare type of hives called angioedema, which produces swelling in large colorless areas, usually around the lips, eyelids, tongue and throat.
rapid swelling in the upper airways can also result, and it can become so severe that breathing is impaired. suffocation is even possible.
years ago, betty had several of these kinds of attacks in which her eyes and face suddenly swelled to a frightening degree. once it happened when we were at a party and we thought it was an allergic reaction to something she had eaten.
angioedema, when it begins to affect breathing, is a medical emergency, vandellen and other mayo doctors warned. writing in a recent issue of the mayo health letter, they said, "report to a hospital emergency room immediately if you have these symptoms. an injection of epinephrine may be necessary to provide relief."
since the party incident, betty has undergone a series of allergy treatments and has not had a recurrence of angioedema, if that's what it was.
i have wondered if it could have been something i said at the party that upset her and caused the dangerous hives.
but vandellen said that those instances in which hives are caused by emotions are not common.
"it is pretty rare for someone to get hives because of another person," he said.
but it could happen, he added.
i'm not sure where all of this leaves howard and me. perhaps we should write to dear abby.

title: NEWBORNS WITH TEETH: IT'S A BABY BOOM!
question_only:
dear readers: recently i volunteered the information that i was born with two teeth and my sister, dear abby, was born with one. a woman wrote that she too was born with a tooth and believed it to be a rare occurrence. she wondered if i knew of any famous people who had been born with teeth.
i had never heard of anyone except my sis and me, so i decided to run a survey. the questions: were you born with teeth? if so, how many? are you famous?
at this moment i am beginning to wonder if anyone in this world was not born with teeth. to date, i've received 42,000 responses, and the cards and letters still are pouring in.
almost 80 percent of the respondents were born with two teeth. almost 17 percent were born with one tooth. two percent were born with three teeth. only 1,000 readers were born with four teeth. ninety percent of those who specified the location said the teeth were in the lower jaw. the survey did not turn up anyone who was famous, although one reader said he was in who's who and had been captain of the high school football team in la crosse, wis.
why are some babies born with teeth? according to dr. paul goldhaber, harvard's dean of dental medicine, teeth develop in utero and the baby born with visible teeth merely exhibits premature development.
how often does this occur? the journal of the american dental association (september, 1984) reported on a study by dentists kates, needleman and holmes. they observed 17,155 newborns and found that 10 were born with teeth. a more casual study involving 11,000 newborns turned up one child with a tooth (or teeth) in every 3,667 births.
here is a sample of what my week has been like:
burlington, vt.: my son was born with two teeth. they were loose but the doctor said to leave them alone. three days later the teeth were gone. i was horrified, thinking he had swallowed them, but we found them under his crib the next day. he is not famous but might be one day. he began to speak in full sentences at 13 months.

title: THE FAME GAME IS DIFFERENT FOR TWINS
question_only:
if you're a twin, here's some bad news for you:
don't plan on ever becoming famous.
the following is based on purely unscientific research, but no one to whom i have talked has ever heard of a twin who has become famous while his or her twin brother or twin sister has remained anonymous. that is, if you have a twin brother or sister, you'd better hope that the two of you become famous together-because there's no chance that you will become famous on your own.
of course, there are cases of twins who have both become very famous. the classic example is those two women from iowa who write under the names of ann landers and dear abby. all they've done is become the most successful newspaper columnists in the world. (i was going to mention the everly brothers next, but they're not twins. they ought to be, though.)
so if you and your twin brother or sister want to become a singing duo or a trapeze act, you just might make it (although, come to think of it,
how famous do trapeze acts really get these days?). if you want to try for fame on your own, though-leaving your twin brother or sister behind-forget it. it's not going to happen.
you may remember, about a year ago, a series of advertisements was launched featuring the brothers and sisters of famous people. the one i recall the most vividly was johnny carson's brother, because he looked a lot like johnny carson. the point of the ad campaign was twofold: (1) to prove that the company in question treated everybody like a star and (2) to save a lot of money by not having to hire the stars themselves. it was a cute campaign. unfortunately, i can't say how effective it was, because i have no idea what product or service it was advertising.
but if you think that the brothers and sisters of famous people have problems, think about the twin brothers and sisters of famous people. in the case of the aforementioned ad campaign, one might imagine that it was the less-famous brother or sister who might have the psychological problem, always wondering why he or she never quite made it. in the case of twins, though, i suspect that it would be the famous member of the pair of twins who would be tormented. which is why there are no famous individual twins.
let's take the most well-known twin in the world: elvis presley. in case you didn't know it, elvis had a twin brother, jesse, who died at birth. (i'm slowly decompressing from graceland; before long, you won't be seeing elvis references here so often. i promise.)
anyway . . . one of the most painful things in elvis presley's life was the loss of jesse at birth. but it could be argued that, if jesse presley had lived, elvis presley would never have become a star. think about it: here's young elvis, touring the south as a 21-year-old rockabilly singer-and here's his twin brother jesse, maybe sitting around the phi delt house at ole miss. jesse would say to his college friends, "yeah, elvis might have been here, too, but he didn't do all that great on his sats."
the point is that stars are stars precisely because they are unique. and twins-even though they aren't the same person, and are doubtless unique in their own minds-don't seem unique to others. they seem to be the same person- especially when they're identical twins.
so if you set out to become a star, and you're a twin, you're always going to be burdened by the fact that there's another version of you running around, looking just like you and talking just like you. you may become a success-you may even become more successful than your twin brother or sister, if that matters to you-but you aren't going to be a star. it would be too confusing to the public.
i apologize for bringing such bad tidings. but it's true; if you're a twin, the best you can hope for is to do better than your twin brother or sister, and let that be enough to satisfy you. a pair of twins like ann and abby come along only once in a generation of so; you can try to be like them, and both become world-famous. but become a star on your own, and leave your twin in the shadows? sorry. it's just not going to happen. that shadow is always going to be there to pull you down.

title: ANY WOMAN CAN BE ABUSE VICTIM
question_only:
dear readers: every day more than 2 million women in this country are abused physically and emotionally in their homes by someone they live with. domestic abuse is the most common violent crime in this country.
every 18 seconds a woman is battered.
any woman can be a victim of abuse: any age, race, culture, sexual preference or class.
abuse takes many forms. it ranges from insults, put-downs and threats, to slaps, punches, choking, rape, stabbing and, all too often, death.
why does a woman stay in an abusive situation? because of . . .
fear: if she leaves he will find her and kill her.
guilt: somehow the abuse was her fault.
shame, embarrassment: she doesn't want friends or family to know, can't admit that the marriage/relationship isn't working.
low self-esteem, helplessness: she feels she can't make it on her own, can't support her children, will never find someone else to "love" her.
she may have no money, no place to go, no help or support from friends or family. she may be physically ill. she might still be hoping he will change and wishing for a "happily ever after" that doesn't exist.
any or all of these factors make it difficult for a battered woman to escape the violence that rules her life.
men who abuse come from every class, race, culture, age and occupation. they can be poor and unemployed or rich and powerful. many were abused as children or witnessed abuse. their anger, insecurity and low self-esteem are expressed through violence and abuse.
domestic violence exists in every culture and society all over the world. it is a shameful part of our history hidden and ignored until the 1970s. it exists because of centuries of sexist attitudes and beliefs that condone and excuse the abuse of women by husbands, lovers, fathers, all men.
some facts
-over 50 percent of sexual assaults take place in a residence of some kind.
-50 to 60 percent are "acquaintance rapes" -- the assailants know or are "friends" or relatives of the victims.
-71 percent of all types of sexual assaults are planned.
-the fbi estimates that only one out of 10 sexual assaults are reported.
-in 93 percent of sexual assaults, the victim and assailant are of the same race and socioeconomic class.
-victims range in age from infancy to their 90s, and every race, class and culture.
any time a woman is coerced or forced into sexual relations without complete voluntary consent, she has been sexually assaulted.
no woman asks to be raped. no woman deserves to be sexually assaulted.
what to do if you are sexually assaulted:
-call the police. they will take you for medical treatment if you need or want it. they will ask for a description of the assailant and the attack. (you do not have to report the assault or press charges, but i recommend it.)
-get medical treatment immediately at an emergency room, clinic or from your personal physician. you may have received internal injuries or been exposed to venereal disease, and there is the possibility of pregnancy.
remember: do not bathe or shower. valuable evidence will be destroyed.
save the clothes you were wearing at the time of the assault.
as soon as you are able, write down as many of the details of the attack as you can remember.

title: FIRE PREVENTION TIPS FOR ALL SEASONS
question_only:
dear readers: next week is fire prevention week, and despite declines, the united states and canada still have the highest fire death rates of all the developed countries of the free world.
the most recent figures (for 1986): in the united states, 5,850 civilians and 113 firefighters died in fires, and approximately 26,825 civilians and 100,900 firefighters were seriously injured. the total loss in property alone came to $6.7 billion. each season has its own special fire hazards. here are some tips for all seasons:
fall: if you enjoy camping, select a tent made of flame-resistant fabric. pack a reliable flashlight with plenty of extra batteries to light the inside of your tent-never use matches or candles. when building a campfire, place it downwind of your tent. and never try to hasten the burning by using gasoline or other flammable liquid starters.
if you use your fireplace, have your chimney professionally cleaned in the fall to make sure it's in good condition for the coming season.
winter: more fires occur during the winter than in any other season. the reasons: home heating and the holiday season.
if you use a portable heater, be sure it is placed away from combustibles-draperies, furniture, paper, etc. remember, the surface heat of some portable heaters may reach 500 degrees, so keep a careful watch on your children and warn them to keep away from heaters. hospitals are treating an increasing number of patients with burns resulting from contact with the outside surface of some portable heaters.
for a merry christmas, choose a christmas tree that does not have shedding needles, and keep it standing in water while it is in the house. if you choose an artificial tree, choose one that is flame-resistant.
after holiday parties, before retiring, check your ashtrays for smoldering cigarette butts, and carefully examine all upholstered chairs and sofas to make sure that no "live" cigarette butts have fallen between the cushions. remember, most house fires occur between 8 p.m. and 8 a.m., when people are sleeping.
spring: take spring cleaning seriously-clean out your attic, basement, garage and workshop. throw out trash, especially combustibles such as rags, newspapers, magazines, boxes and scraps of wood. never smoke while fueling gas-powered lawn mowers or chain saws. if you must store gasoline, store it in a ventilated area in a can designed especially for that purpose. and store oily rags and paint in a cool place in tightly sealed metal containers.
summer: when cooking out, never use flammable liquids near live coals. an explosion or flash fire could result. when you've finished cooking, soak the coals with water and make absolutely sure they're out when you leave. smoldering coals that appear to be "dead" can reignite as much as a day later. if you use a propane gas grill, always have the lighted match in position before turning on the gas.
"play it safe . . . plan your escape!" is this year's theme. some tips for all seasons:
-never smoke in bed.
-never leave invalids or small children alone in the house, not even for "a few minutes."
-never use flammable liquids for dry cleaning indoors.
-have periodic fire drills in your home to be sure everyone knows what to do in case of fire.
-keep easy-to-use fire extinguishers in your kitchen, cottage, back bedrooms and on your boat. invest in smoke detectors, and be sure that they are kept dust-free and in working order.
-the telephone number of your fire department should be taped to every telephone in your house. if it isn't, should a fire occur, don't waste time trying to find it; get out, and call from a neighbor's house. and once you are out, stay out. no treasure is worth risking your life for.

title: WOMEN BERATE MEN IN NEW HITE BOOK ON SEX, LOVE IN '80S
question_only:
"i don't have a vocabulary to tell the pleasure of sleeping alone after sharing a bed with the same man for 30 years. it was heaven. it took months to get used to the sheer joyous ecstasy."
poor men.
every sexist, stupid, selfish, chauvinistic, domineering, leering, lusting, mean, ugly, arrogant, date-raping, down-putting, undercutting thing men do to women is reported, surveyed, dissected and tabulated in that new book being promoted to best-seller status, shere hite's "women and love."
"women and why they hate men" would be a more accurate title for the 922-page collection of quotes and analysis.
"one thing that has always amazed me is that a man can ignore you or treat you shabbily and then expect you to respond to him with love when he wants sex."
the third in hite's trilogy about changing relationships between men and women, the hefty book is based on essay-type answers to a lengthy questionnaire filled out anonymously by 4,500 women recruited through a variety of women's groups and by self- selection.
the methodology provides enough poignant personal stories and complaints about men to fill a decade of daily ann landers and dear abby columns. it is being attacked by critics as unscientific and defended by the author and her supporters as essential to elicit honest feelings.
"i remember crying over problems with my husband. why? because i could never reach him. i could never really communicate with him, never share with him . . . the divorce was like death and rebirth."
but readers are left with the choice of concluding that (1) the survey sample is biased; (2) the author's selection of responses and analyses is prejudiced; or (3) overwhelming numbers of women really feel mistreated and used by men.
hite says, for example, that 84 percent of women are not satisfied emotionally with their relationships with men; 96 percent give men more emotional support than they get; 95 percent report emotional and psychological harassment from men they love; 95 percent say men assume they should come first psychologically in relationships; 93 percent work harder at making relationships work than do men.
the litany of complaints about men goes on and on and on. men distance themselves emotionally and won't talk about problems and feelings. men nag. they use physical violence against women. they expect women to make a relationship work. or they don't want a relationship-just sex. men smother women and usurp their identity.
eighty-five percent of the single women report that most men expect sex on the first date. if a woman refuses, she may be accused to playing games or being stuffy and risks never seeing the guy again. if she does have sex, he may consider her "easy" and not return. eighty percent say they have had the experience of having sex with a man and then never hearing from him again.
"pressure to have sex has been a big problem for women since the phony 'sexual liberation' of the '60s, which made us 'free' to do whatever a man wanted us to do. they all had the gall to assume that now that the moral constraints didn't forbid our having sex, of course we wanted to do it with them, whenever they asked for it."
it's surprising that such a voluminous book about women, men and love would devote only seven pages to the effects of children on love between men and women-only three of the pages positive and happy. but it spends more than 100 pages on gay women and gay relationships.
hite's own prejudices are clear from the short sections of analysis that link the extensive quotes. she often slips into vintage antimale feminist rhetoric. she says women risk marriage and endure its injustices "because the idea of marriage" still holds hope of intimacy and trust, but notes that about half of wives break up their disappointing marriages and many who stay do so in bitterness and disillusionment.
"would it be too simplistic to blame all our problems on the 'male ideology' with its hierarchical and aggressive motifs?" hite asks. she rejects the idea that biology is the root of sex inequality and notes that patriarchy is, after all, "the system underlying all other systems" in society and history.
never mind that millions of women love and live with men in lasting intimacy, with a reasonable degree of equality and happiness. maybe they didn't bother to fill out hite's exhaustive questionnaire or their answers didn't fit hite's theories.
"we no longer believe in the male gods; their power over us has ended." poor men. it isn't easy to adjust to a cultural revolution when it's aimed at you.

i'd like to get this off my chest. it's about time humans stopped referring to acts that people perpetrate as people "acting like animals."
i refer generally to those who describe murders, riots, panics and other catastrophes in which people lose control and are said to be "acting like animals."
i refer specifically to comments regarding a recent ship hijacking when it was said that the terrorists acted like "cowardly animals."
these terrorists and guerrilla acts are not animal in nature. they are human in nature. as one who sees the balance, beauty and meaning of the world in which animals must face life-or-death situations every day just to survive and perpetuate the species, i grossly resent and take offense at these statements.
when was the last time we saw a gorilla hijack a plane? when was the last time we saw a pod of whales hijack an ocean liner? when was the last time we saw a group of animals walk down the street and terrorize the neighborhood? people, in fact, are the terrorists and guerrillas when they go into the animals' element to slaughter them for fur coats, hunting trophies, plumage and all the other atrocious reasons society gives for the gross neglect of respect for life and murder of our fellow creatures inhabiting this world.
if the day ever comes when man comes off his ego trip, maybe he will see just how insignificant he is to the total scheme of things on this tremendous planet in which all creatures share. maybe then, finally, the saying will be turned around to, "they behaved like people."
kathy l. lineaweaver,
clifton park, n.y.

title: 'DEAR' SISTERS AN INSIDE PEEK AT RIVAL TWINS ABBY AND ANN
question_only:
the unauthorized biography of ann landers and abigail van buren by jan pottker and bob speziale dodd, mead, 320 pages, $17.95 dear ann landers by david grossvogel contemporary books, 195 pages, $16.95
love and rivalry. success and betrayal. feuding sisters who can't resist turning everything-from marriage to mink coats, from cars to careers-into a relentless competition.
if you think this sounds like ripe material for ann landers and dear abby, you're right. but this drama hasn't been culled from letters in their advice columns; it's from their own lives.
in "dear ann, dear abby," pottker and speziale spin out the delicious details of the rift, showing how and why eppie lederer (ann) and popo phillips (abby) have spent years trying to outdo each other. in the end, the book proves that sisterhood may indeed be powerful, but it can also be plenty catty.
"i understand why eppie's disturbed," they quote popo as saying. "she wanted to be the first violin in the school orchestra, but i was. she swore she'd marry a millionaire, but i did."
neither lederer nor phillips cooperated with the writing of this unauthorized biography (in fact, the authors note the many roadblocks the sisters threw in their path), but more than 150 of their friends, relatives and associates did. the result is an incredibly juicy story of lives entwined so closely that, over time, their sisterly bond appeared to degenerate into one of backbiting and intrigue.
born and raised in sioux city, ia., the sisters grew up as the incredibly close friedman twins. they dressed alike, they talked alike, they slept in the same single bed, even their names-esther pauline and pauline esther-were identical. the first night they spent away from each other was after their double wedding.
then the trouble started. popo had married into money, something she never failed to point out to everyone, and eppie hadn't. in fact, after several years, the sisters found themselves in the same town, eau claire, wis., with eppie's husband working for popo's. the tension between the twins began to spill into a contest for attention.
for example, there was the time eppie spoke before a red cross meeting. upon hearing how successful her sister's speech was, popo called the secretary of family service and asked to be a featured speaker. then she bought up all the tickets and gave them to her friends.
evidently, the twins' ever-escalating bid for publicity began to rile the publisher of the local paper. "i told them they would be put on a ration," says marshall atkinson of the eau claire leader-telegram. "only one picture in the newspaper every six months. they were very indignant. . . ."
competition turned into outright feuding in 1955, when both sisters started writing advice columns. according to pottker and speziale, eppie was furious that popo became dear abby only three months after she became ann landers.
"after years of being overshadowed by her sister, eppie believed she had achieved something unique and apart from her twin," they write. "she was not prepared for rival syndication from anyone, and especially not popo."
from that point on, the hostility between the sisters escalated, and pottker and speziale, both washington journalists, have documented every detail. for example: - the life magazine article where popo mentioned eppie's nose job, adding that eppie "revealed certain freudian flaws of character by going through with the operation." - eppie's retaliation that popo is "just like a kid who beats a dog until somebody looks, and then she starts petting it." - the eight years when the twins refused to speak to each other, even at the wedding of eppie's daughter, margo. sen. hubert humphrey tried to patch things up by dancing with both sisters at once. it didn't work. - the assessment of william steven, their minneapolis editor, on working with both ann and abby, "one does not cross those babes."
still, there is more to the ann-abby story than feuding twins with identical jobs: how did two '50s-era women propel themselves into high-rolling careers while upholding the sanctity of traditional family roles in print? while pottker and speziale examine that fascinating trajectory through the personalities of ann and abby, author david grossvogel takes a different approach.
in "dear ann landers," grossvogel, a professor of literature and romance languages at cornell, analyzes what he calls "the intimate and changing dialogue" readers have had with landers since 1955.
to that end, grossvogel has read more than 35,000 letters-every one landers ever published, he claims-and divided them into related categories. the result is a sociological compendium of our concerns and values over the last 30-plus years.
that makes it, at times, a fun book to dip into, especially when grossvogel records the details of the raging toilet paper debate. (should the paper come over the top of the roll or under? approximately 15,000 readers had an opinion.) also, there's the national uproar that occurred when landers said that housewives should iron their sheets and towels.
but, all too often, grossvogel's insights are too predictable; most people could guess that sex, drugs and women's rights are bigger issues today than in the 1950s.
still, the book functions nicely as a collection of ann landers' "golden oldies." and there's an interesting interview with landers herself, who says that she has "a visceral feeling about the topics i should take to my readers. . .when i ran across the toilet paper letter, i knew at once it was a subject thousands of people would want to say something about."
that visceral feeling is, of course, what keeps all of ann's and abby's readers-an estimated 90 million daily-tuning in for more. reading their columns is like eavesdropping on a national party line and that, of course, is what both books are all about.

title: TOWELS EXPRESS A MOM'S CONCERN

title: MARINES' SURVIVORS FILL BEIRUT VOID
question_only:
four times a year, in either joan muffler's living room in philadelphia or judy young's kitchen in moorestown, n.j., the two women get together to type up and lay out a newsletter called the beirut connection.
it is national in scope and is eagerly awaited in cities like chicago and los angeles. in small towns like wickenburg, ariz., and gilbertsville, ky. and out in the rural stretches of america-from the western woods in washington state to the eastern woods of maine.
but it is a select few who subscribe, for most of the circulation is made up of families whose sons and husbands were veterans who served in beirut from 1982 to 1984 with the u.s. marine corps; 268 of those men did not come home alive.
muffler's 19-year-old son, john, and young's 22-year-old son, jeff, were killed in the oct. 23, 1983, terrorist bombing of the marine corps headquarters where 241 marines died one sunday morning as they slept.
the newsletter was created by the two mothers so that the men who died on a "peacekeeping mission" in war-torn beirut would not be forgotten. and, young says, so that the families would not feel alone and that all the american veterans of beirut would be "thought of with the 3 r's: respect, reverence and remembrance."
"these boys are our newest veterans," says subscriber james clark, of minong, wis., whose son, randy, was killed in an earlier rocket attack on the marine corps compound at the beirut airport.
"i'm afraid these boys have been pushed aside by the public. i mean forgotten-the ones who died there and the ones who survived," clark says. "they got shot at, but they couldn't fire back. they were targets, but nobody in our government would admit they were targets. they served honorably, but it wasn't a war. what was it, i ask? and what did we ever accomplish? who's even remembering beirut?"
"i remember it well," says john zurakowski, randy clark's best friend in the marines, reflecting on the barracks attack. "at the time, our company was stationed up on the hill at beirut university. it was early sunday morning, and we were on holiday routine. i heard this big explosion that woke me up, and i went and sat down on some stairs and smoked a cigarette. a guy with binoculars came down from the building roof and said, 'you know the battalion headquarters that you can see from here? it's not there anymore.' "
zurakowski, who was 19 when he was sent to beirut and is now out of the marines, says that while it was right in principle for the marines to go there, the rules of ducking and not shooting back confused him and his buddies.
"we could have made a difference, but it didn't work," he says. "the lebanese army had no discipline. they would smoke and drink all night while they were on duty. we often got artillery rounds fired at us with no fuses, and we figured it was the lebanese army shooting at us so we would get mad and do their fighting for them. it sort of made you wonder what was going on there."
"none of us understood what was going on in beirut . . . not really," muffler says. "the parents all got letters that said, 'everything was okay, don't worry, can't wait to get home.'
"then came the explosion, and our sons were killed. i found nine families in philadelphia who'd lost their sons, and we all got together in december of 1983 and it felt so good to talk to each other.
"we had nothing of our sons. no pictures. no scrapbooks. no articles of clothing because it all went up with the building. so we thought of contacting other families and asked the government to give us their names. the government said they could not because of the privacy act."
a friend suggested that the two women write columnist dear abby to appeal to other families who were spread out all across the country.
abby called their houses and put the message in her column, and the letters flooded in from everywhere-from mothers, wives, sisters and brothers, from marines who served in beirut and from those who survived the explosion.
"the letters were so touching, so passionate, and the writers of these letters were in such need to communicate with somebody else who'd had the beirut experience that we put together the beirut connection," muffler says.
the newsletter has been growing ever since. it now goes to 38 states, jamaica and puerto rico and has a subscription list of 402. families used to pay for their subscriptions by sending stamps. they now pay $3 a year.
families write of small plaques that have gone up in their hometowns in memory of the "boys from beirut," gossip is passed, photographs are exchanged, poems are shared.
a grief-stricken wife writes of her marine husband who killed himself shortly after his return from beirut. a young former marine wounded in the explosion writes of how his state does not consider him a veteran wounded in war because beirut was not a war, it was merely a mission.
"the newsletter has been therapy for all of us," muffler says. "and i think we all feel better for it. but we are going to have a new emphasis now. that is for the survivors.
"they are still young and they don't talk much yet about what they saw there. probably because it hurts. i had a friend of my son who wrote me several letters. he always sounded so down in those letters, and i asked him why. he responded that he felt he died with his friends. then he packed his things and moved, and i've never heard from him again.
"the ones who lived, the veterans of beirut, need to be heeded, too . . . like the rest of america's living veterans," young says. "we don't want these men to feel forgotten or excluded."

title: SMOKEOUT CAN HELP CLEAR THE AIR
question_only:
tomorrow will mark the 11th annual great american smokeout, a one-day campaign to encourage smokers to quit smoking for 24 hours-just to prove they can do it.
the idea was conceived by the american cancer society, which insists that anyone who can live without a cigarette for 24 hours can quit forever.
during the 1986 great american smokeout, a record-breaking 23.8 million smokers tried to quit for the day. this represents more than 43 percent of the nation's 54.5 million smokers.
lung cancer is the no. 1 cause of cancer death among both women and men. an estimated 92,000 men and 44,000 women will die of lung cancer in 1987. breast cancer used to be the biggest killer for women-now it's lung cancer!
a congressional study has reported that health costs from the adverse effects of smoking have reached a new high of $100 billion a year in increased medical bills and lost productivity. the loss in death and disability cannot be measured. (and how does one measure the amount of heartache, remorse and guilt suffered as a result of a preventable, self-induced tragedy?)
what about "secondhand" smoke? is it actually damaging to non-smokers to be in the presence of those who are smoking? yes! furthermore, studies reveal that the children of smokers are more prone to lung problems and allergies than are children of non-smokers.
for years i have begged my young readers, "if you smoke, quit now. if you don't smoke, don't start!" yet an estimated 3,000 to 5,000 kids light up for the first time every day. why? peer pressure, no doubt.
quitting "cold turkey" is the hardest way to quit, but my readers have told me it's the most effective, and in the long run, the easiest way. cutting down is less traumatic, but the temptation to smoke is often too powerful to resist while smoking just one, two or three cigarettes a day.
those who are heavily addicted may require professional help to break the habit.
so, if you're hooked on cigarettes, and have been telling yourself, "one of these days i'm going to quit," why not start tomorrow-just for 24 hours?
it won't be easy, but it will be the best thanksgiving present you can give yourself-and those who love you.
p.s. a favor, please? if you quit tomorrow even for 24 hours, i want to hear from you. then write again and let me know how long you were able to stay clean. good luck. keep me posted. i care.

title: BE THANKFUL ON THANKSGIVING DAY
question_only:
dear readers: an update on my traditional thanksgiving column:
tomorrow is thanksgiving day, so take a few minutes to think about what you have to be thankful for.
how's your health? not so good? well, thank god you've lived this long. a lot of people haven't. you're hurting? thousands-maybe millions-are hurting more. (have you ever visited a veterans hospital? or a hospital for crippled children?)
if you awakened this morning and were able to hear the birds sing, use your vocal cords to utter human sounds, walk to the breakfast table on two good legs and read the newspaper with two good eyes (or even one), praise the lord! a lot of people couldn't.
how's your pocketbook? thin? well, most of the world is a lot poorer. no pensions. no welfare. no food stamps. no social security. no medicare. in fact, one-third of the people in the world will go to bed hungry tonight.
are you lonely? the way to have a friend is to be one. if nobody calls you, pick up the phone and call somebody. go out of your way to do something nice for somebody. it's a sure cure for the blues.
are you concerned about your country's future? hooray! our system has been saved by such concern. concern for fair play under the law. if you don't like your elected officials, you can go to work and vote them out of office. we still have the soapbox and the ballot box. or would you rather be in central america, ethiopia or afghanistan?
freedom rings! you can still worship at the church of your choice, or not worship at all. you can cast a secret ballot, and even criticize your government without fearing a knock on the head or a knock on your door in the middle of the night.
and if you want to live under a different system, goodbye and good luck! you are free to go. there are no walls or fences to keep you here.
as a final thought, i'll repeat my thanksgiving prayer; perhaps you will want to use it at your table tomorrow:
o, heavenly father: we thank thee for food and remember the hungry.
we thank thee for health and remember the sick.
we thank thee for friends and remember the friendless.
we thank thee for freedom and remember the enslaved.
may these remembrances stir us to service
that thy gifts to us may be used for others. amen.
have a wonderful thanksgiving, and may god bless you and yours. love, abby
an afterthought: want an instant high? the surest cure for the post- holiday blues is to do something nice for someone. why not call someone who lives alone and invite him (or her) over for dinner?
better yet, call and say, "i'm coming to get you, and i'll see that you get home." (many older people don't drive, and those who do don't like to go out alone after dark.)

title: ABBY'S TIPS FOR HOLIDAY GIFT GIVING
question_only:
dear readers: well, are the christmases getting closer together or does it just seem that way? it's time to start preparing for the holidays again, so do yourselves a favor and do your christmas or hanukkah shopping early.
here's my annual-slightly revised-column on holiday shopping.
if you're wondering what to give aunt olivia or grandpa, who doesn't go out much, let me tell you what not to give them:
forget dusting powder, after-shave and cologne. (they probably have several unopened boxes gathering dust on their closet shelves.)
grandpa doesn't need another necktie, and aunt sylvia doesn't really want any more brooches, necklaces, bracelets or earrings.
with the price of groceries so high, older folks who live alone on a fixed income would be delighted to receive a basket of goodies. include small cans of salmon, chicken, ham, tuna, fruit, instant coffee, tea bags, crackers, cookies and instant soup mixes.
older people who live in confined quarters do not need more "things" that are ornamental only. don't send music boxes, statuettes or other bric-a- brac.
a truly thoughtful gift: postcards and some lined stationery with envelopes and a generous supply of postage stamps. (enclose some felt-tip pens, too.)
a handy gift: an assortment of greeting cards for all occasions, so that they, too, can send birthday, anniversary, graduation, get-well and condolence cards to others.
don't give a gift of clothing unless you're absolutely sure the size is right.
if you're tempted to pass along a scarf, purse, wallet or some little doodad you received three christmases ago, please don't; the recipient will probably find it just as useless as you did. (besides, you might get it back the year after next.)
if someone on your gift list is living on a pension, a check for any amount would be far more appreciated than some useless little trinket. another thoughtful gift would be a year's subscription to a newspaper or magazine you are sure he or she will enjoy.
if you buy a gift on sale, be sure it's appropriate, since if the recipient tries to exchange it, he will be told, "sorry, sale merchandise is not returnable."
never give a pet to anyone unless you're absolutely sure a pet is wanted and will be properly cared for. and if you want to delight someone who considers his pet a "member of the family," include a tin or two of cat or dog food for the pet.
don't give wine or liquor unless you're sure the recipients imbibe. candy, nuts and fruitcake make wonderful gifts for those who aren't counting calories, but please have compassion for those who are, and lead them not into temptation. also remember that many older people have difficulty chewing hard candies and nuts.
instead of giving someone a gift with permission to "take it back and exchange it if it's not what you want," save yourself (and them) time and effort by giving gift certificates in the first place.
for those who maintain their own homes and apartments, consider a gift certificate for other types of service needed-window washing and rug cleaning. and don't forget certificates for the barber shop, beauty parlor, taxi rides or dinner out to a fine restaurant. and (don't laugh) a trip to the podiatrist!
holiday time can be depressing for people who are alone, so if you know someone who might be alone and lonely, give him (or her) the best gift of all- an invitation to have a holiday meal with you and your family. loneliness is the ultimate poverty. love, abby

title: A BIT OF ADVICE OVER TEA
question_only:
at precisely half past four, just as the ladies were lifting their limoges teacups to their lips and sipping their darjeelings, eppie lederer pounded out a few chords on the piano keys. she wanted everyone's attention.
"ladies, ladies, will you all please find a seat and we'll have a few words."
the chatter continued. dear ann landers tried again.
setting her watercress roll on the edge of her saucer, she called out: "hellooo ladies." as a hush fell over the room, eppie squeezed her arm tight around her 17-minutes-younger twin sister, popo phillips, who is known to millions of readers as abigail van buren of dear abby fame.
yes, the sisters twin stood before a crowd of 50 women friday afternoon in eppie's east lake shore drive drawing room, kissed each other on the lips and told tales of staying up giggling till 4 a.m. the night before and together "killing" three-quarters of a pralines 'n' cream ice cream pie before shuffling off to bed.
eppie, you see, threw a little tea for popo for popo has just compiled a booklet for her readers called "dear abby's favorite recipes."
as eppie explained to her guests: "i read a squib in her column that she was coming out with this booklet, not a book, and i thought, 'well i have parties for my friends' books all the time; so why not a tea for my sister.' i called her up and she said, 'i think that would be terrific.'
"at first," popo jumped in to correct her sister, "i said, 'are you crazy?' "
eppie went right ahead. "i really got my list out of best friends. i called 52 and 50 said yes. my sister said, 'four o'clock tea, who will come?'
"i said, 'everyone. the women will do their shopping at saks or somewhere and then come by.' and now, i want to introduce you to my twin sister, popo. as betty corbally said just now when she walked in the door, 'you two must've been the cutest little things in the buggy.' "
with that, the sisters squeezed hands, and popo said a few words before the ladies returned to the petite mocha eclairs:
"when you tell people that you've met eppie's twin sister, abby, they will say, 'do they speak?' do we speak? we don't shut up. i can attest to that."
the ladies chuckled. sterling spoons tinkled against china. the clock on the mantle chimed five times. everyone soon departed, charmed by the genteel twosome who hailed from sioux city, ia., and went on to advise the world.
goodman blesses everyone with 'christmas carol'
it must be time for mistletoe and holly and stories of scrooge.
it simply must be because wednesday night at the goodman theatre a whole audience of kiddies were nestled snug in their seats, many of them boosted for a better view by virtue of folded raincoats or overstuffed briefcases. and while a whole cast of crachits and christmas ghosts-past, present and yet to come-unspooled "a christmas carol" for the 10th year in a row, a whole gallery of little voices spilled forth a commentary that sometimes rivaled the action on stage.
when someone on stage called the crachits "poor and destitute," a 5- year-old front and center echoed to her father, "poor and what?" when clouds of fog rolled onto the stage from the wings, a 6-year-old wondered loudly, "how do they do that?"
one of the most curious in the house-one whose questions kept a whole knot of viewers giggling around him-was max adler, 3. max's father is a theater critic, and young max exhibited that he, too, could question the theater.
"this is his first big show. he doesn't know the conventions yet, like how to keep quiet," said max's slightly blushing father, tony, as he followed his son from his seat to the coke line at the end of act 1.
no matter, though, all the chatter from the house. it's all a part of the play.
"thank god people procreate," said irving markin, chairman of the chicago theatre group's board of trustees. "it gives us a market each year for this show. you expect this from the goodman. it's a part of the season."
wednesday's night's opening of "a christmas carol" was also the 10th anniversary party of the chicago theatre group inc., which has supported the goodman since it broke from the art institute in 1977.
and although the tuxedoed guests of ctg enjoyed a candle-lit meal before the play, it was the cast party following ebenezer's enlightenment that really hopped with the holiday spirit.
besides max, who was not to be slowed despite the near-midnight hour, there was 5-year-old kevin duda, who got time off from kindergarten to play tiny tim for the next 30 shows and who had nothing to say about being a star except that it was "fine."
while the little ones darted in and out of the crowd and occasionally found themselves scooped up to big peoples' shoulders, mr. scrooge, played for the ninth season by william j. norris, sat limp in a chair, sipping on ice water, and mused about the impact of the story he calls a "family classic."
"schuunk, it gets me in the heart every time," he said, striking a fist to his chest. "my hope is that everybody is touched. it's not a children's story; it's a family story. my hope is that parents don't drop children off and take a two-hour vacation. i come back every year to do scrooge. why? i gotta get it right."
they're 8 perfect little kids
jeanne farnan wandered wide-eyed about the teak-paneled conrad hilton suite on the 29th floor of the chicago hilton and towers tuesday night. the 4- foot-4 6th grader from bridgeport catholic academy could not conceal her amazement at her surroundings.
she rubbed her palm over the medieval tapestry hanging from the wall. she bent her neck all the way back to where her hairbow touched her angel's wings so she could count the crystals in the chandelier. she stood on her tiptoes so she could eye the deep-fried shrimp sizzling in the sterling silver chafing dish.
then she discovered the winding staircase behind the buffet table, and she could not help but whisper: "the bedrooms must be down there. if they pay this much money for the apartment, they're not going to sleep on the couch."
so went 11-year-old jeanne farnan's debut with chicago's swankiest circles.
for the 50 or so ceos and their wives milling about the penthouse suite before the boys and girls clubs of chicago annual award dinner, this was just another ho-hum soiree where shrimp is supposed to be oversized, champagne is expected to be free-flowing and, of course, all the best baubles are brought out from the bank vault.
but for jeanne and seven other pint-sized club members invited to escort the eight women being honored as chicagoans of the year, this was downright unbelievable.
even though the winged collar on 11-year-old eddie robertson's rented tuxedo was "itching like crazy," and even though jeanne was "scared as heck" about singing the national anthem in front of lyric opera's ardis krainik (never mind the other 1,038 guests), the kids agreed that being at the party was a whole lot better than being at home with "moonlighting" and a plate of spaghetti-os.
"i've never seen so much jewelry in my entire life," jeanne whispered, continuing her social commentary half hidden behind one of the suite's 12- foot-high chintz curtains. "last year my teacher got married and she had a diamond and i thought it was really huge. you come here and it's like it was a grain of sand."
one other thing jeanne observed: "everything here is so critical. you have to act the right way, talk the right way, eat the right way. you can't say things you'd usually say. lord knows, you have to be perfect."

title: PARENTS UPSET BY COLLEGIATE MORALS

title: WOMAN WITH 2 SUITORS WANTS BOTH!

after we had placed our order, roger became very fussy, so we tried to comfort him by holding him. my husband even took him outside for a while. when he brought him back, he started to cry very loudly again, so we thought if we put him in his car seat beside us, he might settle down by himself.

title: HE LIKES HER-BUT NOT HER KIDS!

title: TWIN BEDS CAN IMPROVE A MARRIAGE

question_only: in answer to the "waitress in banff" who asks why people seem to prefer "dirty" tables: they don't necessarily prefer "dirty" tables; the choice tables are occupied more than the others. and which tables are preferred? studies have shown, and restaurant designers have long known, that people will fill a restaurant in a predictable order. people like to have a wall at their backs. they don't like their backs exposed. restaurants tend to fill outer walls first, then window walls, and finally-and only if there is no other choice-center tables. fred maslan, seattle

title: WIFE LEARNS THAT RATS SURVIVE EVEN WHEN CORNERED

re the "lady" who asked if she should send her ex-lover's love letters to his wife:
four years ago, after 12 years of what i thought was a perfect marriage, i learned that my husband was having a long-distance affair with a woman every other weekend. he had lied to her, saying he wasn't married. he wrote love letters to both of us! in his letters to me he said he loved me, couldn't bear to lose me but was in the clutches of "this other woman." meanwhile, he continued to see her every other weekend.

title: LITTLE'S CHANGED FOR FREE AGENTS
question_only:
hawkshaw here has been attempting to offer some preliminary conclusions on the signing of free agents, which, at first glance, seems to be going apace-seven players have made new connections; also, to report if there has been progress in the awarding of damages to the players for the their union's successful 1985 collusion grievance, an arbitrator having determined the owners were guilty of conspiring to prevent a free market.
second things first:
at the winter meetings in dallas the week before last, the members of the owners' player relations committee met for two hours. among other things a settlement was discussed. no vote, no agreement, only talk. the result of our survey produced the following:
one owner acknowledged $10 million was mentioned, but nothing higher.
a second owner acknowledged $15 million was mentioned, but nothing higher.
a third owner acknowledged $20 million was mentioned, but nothing higher.
reminds me of the dear abby column when a woman, who was looking for a husband, said she had been dating a stockbroker. on their first date, he said he was 61 years old; second date, he said he was 59; on the third, he dropped it to 57. what should she do?
abby's reply: when he gets to 55, sell!
all of the owners offered these figures with the understanding they would remain anonymous. this is because of the traditional cloak of silence. to speak publicly not only would endanger relations with their fellow owners but invite the possibility of disciplinary action by comissioner peter ueberroth.
a call was put through to don fehr, the executive director of the major league players association. going high, i said, mr. fehr, how does $20 million hit you?
his reply:
"their proposals have had to do with a package settlement for both years-'85 and '86 (the identical '86 grievance is now being heard)-but we haven't reached the stage of seriously discussing numbers (dollars), because the association cannot settle these cases until there is a real market for the current free agents. and in our opinion, there isn't a free market."
the translation:
if the owners reach agreement on a settlement, which isn't likely, the union will say, in effect, "whoa now! we want to see what happens this year." which means arbitrator tom roberts, eventually, will decide (without realistic recommendations from either side) the extent of the penalty. roberts' decision could come next spring, next summer, maybe next christmas, further evidence the wheels of justice move slowly.
as for the 1987 free agents, there has been the following movement, in alphabetical order:
- outfielder brett butler from cleveland to san francisco.
- outfielder bob dernier, cubs to philadelphia.
- outfielder chili davis, san francisco to california.
- outfielder mike davis, oakland to los angeles.
- outfielder dave henderson, san francisco to oakland (to be announced).
- infielder vance law, montreal to cubs.
- pitcher david palmer, allanta to philadelphia.
a total of 16 free agents have re-signed with their former clubs, or have agreed to salary arbitration, which is the same as re-signing, the only difference being an arbitrator will determine their 1988 pay. they are:
- pitcher juan berenguer, minnesota.
pitcher gene garber, kansas city.
pitcher mark clear, milwaukee.
outfielder dave collins, cincinnati.
outfielder ken griffey, atlanta.
catcher mike heath, detroit.
pitcher tommy john, yankees.
pitcher dave lapointe, white sox.
outfielder lee mazzilli, mets.
outfielder jerry mumphrey, cubs
pitcher joe price, san francisco.
pitcher dave righetti, yankees.
pitcher bryn smith, montreal.
pitcher frank tanana, detroit.
infielder manny trillo, cubs.
pitcher mike witt, california.
together, 23, or approximately one-third of the 76 free agents, are accounted for. is the union's fehr satisfied with the early results?
"no, i'm not satisified," he said. "you just can't look at whether somebody moves or signs with his former club. what you have to ask is, has there been meaningful competition for free agents? or is it 'controlled collusion'? there is no doubt the clubs will not be as blatant as in the past. overall, i would have to say we have not seen a free market. in almost all instances the players who signed with new clubs were not wanted by their former clubs."
whatever, crunch time is still two weeks away. midnight jan. 8 is the deadline for the retaining clubs to sign their free agents who have rejected arbitration. a half-dozen extremely attractive players, all-stars all, are in this group.
alive but spending christmas out in the cold are third baseman gary gaetti, minnesota; first baseman jack clark, st. louis; infielder paul molitor, milwaukee; and pitchers jack morris, detroit; charlie liebrandt, kansas city; and dave smith, houston.
the competition for these players should determine the extent of the free market. until then, hawkshaw reserves judgment.

title: A LOOK BACK AT 1987, FROM THE BAKKERS TO BORK
question_only:
dear readers: what a year!
it was the last curtain call for such luminaries as fred astaire, jackie gleason, ray bolger, danny kaye, robert preston, james coco, lee marvin, lorne greene, randolph scott, geraldine page, hermione gingold and liberace.
we will no longer swing and sway with sammy kaye-or woody herman, either. and a final drum roll for the incomparable buddy rich. remember rudy vallee, whose theme song was "my time is your time"? well, his time was up in '87. and there was no overtime for ohio state's irascible football coach, woody hayes.
exit legendary beauties rita hayworth, mary astor, madeleine carroll and pola negri. and farewell to mervyn leroy, john huston, david susskind and claire booth luce. ditto for andy warhol, who transformed a campbell's tomato soup can into a lucrative work of art.
alf landon, the crusty republican governor of kansas who ran against franklin roosevelt in 1936, died at 100. california had an earthquake. cybill shepherd had twins. dolly parton went from a 44d to a 34b.
shucks, tom selleck got married. so did tom cruise. sylvester stallone's rocky marriage was ko'd, and johnny carson, who said he'd never marry again, did.
the cabinet lost one of its best when secretary of commerce malcolm baldrige was killed by a horse in a freak accident. and william casey, chief honcho of the troubled cia, died, leaving many unanswered questions. naturally.
gary hart lost face. donna rice gained recognition. jessica hahn fell from grace. little jessica mcclure fell down a well, but, praise the lord, she was rescued, and the whole world rejoiced.
ollie north won the hearts of america when, during the iran-contra hearings, he admitted to lying, withholding information and shredding evidence.
costa rica's president oscar arias sanchez won the nobel peace prize for his plan on how to restore peace to central america. the prospects for world peace are looking brighter as we prepare (as i write this) to welcome mikhail and raisa gorbachev.
the minnesota twins won the world series. jim and tammy faye bakker lost their multimillion-dollar ptl ministry, their his-and-hers rolls-royces and all their homes and are now living in malibu in a modest little shack that rents for $7,000 a month.
jerry falwell, who temporarily took over the bakkers' ptl (to "save" it), gave it up. pat robertson turned in his collar and announced that he was running for president. mario cuomo announced that he was not.
oral roberts told his flock on national television that if they didn't cough up $8 million in 60 days, the lord would call him home. (the smith bros. couldn't have coughed up the money faster.)
president reagan pitched judge bork for the supreme court. the senate yelled foul. strike one! second batter up: judge douglas ginsburg. strike two!
elizabeth taylor celebrated her 55th birthday. the constitution celebrated its 200th.
norman lear got married. diana ross got pregnant and had a son. fawn hall got arrested-for eating a banana in a metro station in washington, d.c. (she's appealing it.)
in october the stock market took the worst nosedive since the crash of '29, but "nobody" got hurt because "everybody" said he saw it coming and sold in august. oh, sure!
bring on 1988-with the olympics and the elections. there's a lot to look forward to! love, abby.

title: BULLS' COLLINS LOOKING FOR A LITTLE ADVICE
question_only:
good friends keep in touch.
according to doug collins, he and his good buddy mike fratello were burning up the long-distance lines earlier this season.
in fact, after collins was named coach of the month for leading the bulls to a 10-3 record in november, there was a congratulatory call from atlanta coach fratello.
that was then. the bulls were hot; the hawks were not. this is now. the bulls have lost four in a row; the hawks have won seven of eight.
when collins spots fratello tuesday night before the bulls and hawks wage war above the stadium's rims, he is going to give his good buddy a little grief.
"wait 'til i see him," collins said with a smile. "when he was going bad, i listened to his problems and tried to encourage him. but now that he's okay, and we're struggling, i haven't heard from him. i played ann landers for him? now, where's my dear abby? where's mike fratello now?
"i get up in the morning now to get a cup of coffee at the convenience mart and it's like, i pull my coat collar up, duck my head and tug my hat down real low over my face. i sneak around. before, in a loud voice, it was, 'hey, everyone, how are you? i'm doing fine, just ask!' "
"we've struggled so hard to win each game that it's taken extra effort on the coach's part," said fratello. "i've been staying up late at night looking at films, burning the midnight oil, and i wasn't sure if doug wanted me to call him at 5 a.m.
"we are definitely going to get together. i was going to talk to him at the game because i deal better with people in person. tell doug i brought him his christmas present and i hope he's got one for me."
fratello might share with collins his method of pulling a team out of the doldrums. the hawks started slowly, losing to the bulls at the omni, which is still their only loss at home. back then, fratello said his team was out of sync and struggling to put its game together. his mood was patient, like that of an experienced trainer waiting for a thoroughbred to find its kentucky derby legs. win or lose, at some time tuesday, collins will probably seek encouragement from his friend.
"mike fratello is a great guy to have in the league as a coach," collins said. "he is so supportive of everyone in the league. he is president of the coaches association, and does whatever he can to help other coaches."
collins pointed out that atlanta, boston and the los angeles lakers all went through slumps of varying degrees and are still residing near the top of the national basketball association.
"but the difference between us and the hawks is one of experience to youth," collins said. "their team has been together a little longer than us. right now, our morale is down, very low. the guys have lost a lot of confidence. we'll need a lot of encouragement from that stadium crowd tuesday night. i hope they get behind us."
it would help if the real michael jordan reappeared. the slumping superstar wants to break loose from his 11-for-37 shooting of the last two games that netted a total of 33 points.
"i've got to keep playing hard and keep shooting," jordan said. "i can't get down on myself and not shoot the jumper. i took some extra shooting in practice today and concentrated on a few things. it felt like my jumper was back.

many years ago my husband and i moved to a small town in south carolina. i started attending church regularly, but my husband didn't care to go to church, so i went alone.
every sunday morning when i would arrive at the church, the minister would ask me the same question: "where is your husband this morning?" he usually asked this question in a tone loud enough for others to hear, which i found very embarrassing. after a year or so, i quit going to that church and joined another one.
i've been told by other women that they have experienced the same kind of humiliation when they go to church without their husbands, so maybe if you ran this in your column, the ministers who embarrass wives in this manner would quit doing it.
what advice have you for wives who are always asked this question but find it inconvenient to change churches? carolina churchgoer

title: WIFE SHOULD GIVE MINISTER THE WORD ABOUT TACT
question_only:
i am a woman who recently went to work for a well-known national firm. one of the male employees walked up to me and said, "do you want to hear a cute joke?"
i asked, "is it dirty?" to which he replied, "not for an adult as sophisticated as you."
i smiled and countered with, "i may not be as sophisticated as you think i am, so let's forget the joke, okay?"
he looked startled, and i could see that he was offended. the word soon got around that "the new woman" is a prude. i am not really a prude, but i don't care for dirty jokes. do you think i was wrong to respond as i did? or should i have let him tell me the joke, pretended to enjoy it and let it go at that? newcomer

title: SMOKE IS CLOUDING MARRIAGE PLANS
question_only:
my fiance and i have had a loving and honest relationship for three years. i'm 32 and he's 40. about a year ago i had a nagging cough, so he said if i quit smoking, he would. (we were both fairly heavy smokers.) we both agreed to quit-cold turkey. it wasn't easy, but i did.
at thanksgiving i suspected that he had been sneaking smokes because when i kissed him, i tasted cigarettes, but i didn't want to believe that he was lying to me. when his hair and clothes consistently smelled of tobacco, i confronted him and he admitted that he was still smoking "a little."
i said, "either you're smoking or you're not," and i refused to kiss him until he quit.
he said he needed "time" to quit again. abby, i love this man, but i will not marry him as long as he is smoking.
he says i am making too big a deal of it. am i? heartbroken in yakima

title: SMOKE IS CLOUDING MARRIAGE PLANS
question_only:
i am 38, divorced and have no children. for 2 1/2 years i have been involved with a 45-year-old man who has been married for 20 years, has four teenagers and is catholic. he has allowed no room in his life for anybody but himself, and he's jealous of everything-including my telephone.
all he talks about is divorce, how much he loves me, how much he doesn't love his wife and how he wishes he never had the kids. several months ago i refused to see him anymore and told him i wanted us to get on with our lives elsewhere. then he told his wife about us, moved out of their house and got himself an apartment. (he told his wife he was living with another guy.) he begged me to move in with him, but i needed some time alone for a while. now he says "maybe" he can get a divorce. he says his wife will never ask for one because of their religion, and he himself thinks divorce is immoral, but he may consider eternity in hell in order to be with me now.
this man has admitted to four other relationships prior to ours. (one lasted five years and the woman divorced her husband for him!)
i have never asked him to get a divorce to begin with. is he using his religion to continue eating from a "side dish" throughout his life, or does he really love me? and what should i do about him? side dish

title: TEACHERS TOUCHED BY GIFTS OF LOVE
question_only:
as school teachers at an elementary school, we object to the attitude of "reluctant gift collector" who belittled those "no. 1 teacher" mugs, plaques and pins received from students. the teacher said, "a gift certificate for a free meal would be much more appreciated."
how can this teacher be an example to his/her students when he/she can't appreciate the love and admiration they put into those so-called "useless gimcracks"?
we gratefully accept all gifts from our students as priceless treasures, and we proudly display them in our classrooms and homes. these gifts let us know that we are actually doing our jobs as educators, not only dispensing knowledge, but teaching the future generations how to be human.
let "reluctant gift collector" have the 20 or 30 gift certificates for a meal out-we'd rather have the love! teachers at cottonwood, casa grande, ariz.

title: COUPLES SHOULD LEARN TO LIVE ALONE

she has no club to go to, no special interests, no hobbies, no close women friends-in fact, she's a very boring person to be around. all she does is moan about her loss and watch tv.

title: GIRLFRIEND FEELS LIKE A STRAY NEAR MINISTER'S FLOCK
question_only:

he has been married twice and was hurt both times. he has teenage daughters. i was married once and have three small children. i am a respectable woman, and i work outside my home.
now the problem: we've been seeing each other for more than two years and have kept our relationship a secret because he's a baptist minister and fears that if his congregation learns that he has a girlfriend, they might kick him out of his church. he has been the pastor there for many years.
to further complicate things, his daughters don't want any woman close to their daddy. they give him a hard time at home and snub me at church. i see him only at church and on rare occasions when our kids aren't home and neither one of us has to work. it's hard for me to deal with caring for him and not being able to be with him. i don't want him to lose his church, and i don't want to lose him. what can we do? lonely lady

title: THOUGHTS ON SIN, FROM FANTASY TO FOLLOW-THROUGH

title: A CHANCE TO REBUILD SOME BRIDGES
question_only:
dear readers: are you holding a grudge? don't feel guilty. many of us are. but we need not hold it forever. did you know that there is an international forgiveness week? well, neither did i until last year, when alice parenti of fresno, calif., wrote to tell me about it.
it's from feb. 1 through feb. 6. robert muller, former assistant secretary-general of the united nations, wrote this piece for international forgiveness week: decide to forgive
decide to forgive
for resentment is negative
resentment is poisonous
resentment diminishes and devours the self.
be the first to forgive,
to smile and to take the first step,
and you will see happiness bloom
on the face of your human brother or sister.
be always the first
do not wait for others to forgive.
for by forgiving
you become the master of fate
the fashioner of life
the doer of miracles.
to forgive is the highest
most beautiful form of love.
in return you will receive
untold peace and happiness.
here is the program for achieving a truly forgiving heart:
sunday: forgive yourself.
monday: forgive your family.
tuesday: forgive your friends and associates.
wednesday: forgive across economic lines within your own nation.
thursday: forgive across cultural lines within your own nation.
friday: forgive across political lines within your own nation.
saturday: forgive other nations.
only the brave know how to forgive. a coward never forgives. it is not in his nature.

title: SQUALLING BABIES ARE NOT WELCOME

title: SMALL SHIPS APPRECIATE LETTERS, TOO!
question_only:
i'm not on an aircraft carrier. in fact, i wish i were- spending six months aboard a carrier would be fun. they have video game rooms, snack bars, live uso shows and they receive operation dear abby iii mail. my ship is the smallest in the navy, a guided missile destroyer. i realize it is impossible to get "operation" mail to every ship under way at christmas. i just would like people to stop and think about us-the ones who, for six months, live in a world that is 400 feet long and 40 feet wide. a world that rocks and vibrates constantly. a world where 300 people live and work. it's a place where you forget what day it is. those of us on "small boys" have little time off, and when we do, where can we go?
we are the ones who protect our valuable carriers, recover downed pilots or men overboard. we live with the knowledge that our job is to get between the carrier and the incoming torpedo (or missile); we take the hit so the carrier can continue to fight. we're also the ones who escort tankers in the persian gulf. we've been there since the crisis began.
just a short while back, we were up at 5 a.m. to refuel the ship, then at noon we unloaded ammunition. by 3 p.m. we finished working, and realized that it was thanksgiving day! i have been separated from my wife for two months- only four more to go and we'll be a family again.
abby, i'm not complaining. i love my country. but next christmas, when i am a civilian, my family and i will take a minute or two to think about, and maybe pray for, the guys out there on large ships and small, keeping americans respected and free, at any cost. counting the days in the i.o.
